slot.brief: Figure showing phenol treated with dilute HNO3 vs concentrated HNO3 — ask for the product(s) and a comparison of mononitration vs picric acid formation.

stem: In the reactions shown in the figure, phenol is treated separately with dilute HNO3 and concentrated HNO3. The products X and Z respectively are:

verdicts.working: The –OH group activates the ring and directs substitution to ortho and para positions. Dilute HNO₃ gives o- and p-nitrophenol; concentrated HNO₃ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

working:
Phenol has an OH group that strongly activates the ring. Dilute HNO3 causes electrophilic mononitration at ortho and para positions, giving o- and p-nitrophenol. Concentrated HNO3 with H2SO4 causes trinitration at the two ortho positions and the para position, forming 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).

Independent check: The –OH group activates the ring and directs substitution to ortho and para positions. Dilute HNO₃ gives o- and p-nitrophenol; concentrated HNO₃ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid).
solution: The –OH group activates the benzene ring and directs electrophilic substitution to the ortho and para positions. Dilute $HNO_3$ gives o- and p-nitrophenol, while concentrated $HNO_3$ gives 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid); hence (D).
